s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive ataxia with spasms and myoclonus
key_facts: Difficulty with gait progressed after cessation of alcohol use
Throat spasms do not affect speech or eating
Normal genetic testing for spinocerebellar ataxia types 1, 2, 3, 6, and 12
Severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy on MRI brain without contrast

raw.syndrome_frame: Progressive ataxia with spasms and myoclonus
key_facts: Difficulty with gait progressed after cessation of alcohol use
Throat spasms do not affect speech or eating
Normal genetic testing for spinocerebellar ataxia types 1, 2, 3, 6, and 12
Severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy on MRI brain without contrast

shortlist.label: spinocerebellar ataxia
shortlist.why_kept: 20-year history of progressive ataxia and severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy on MRI

shortlist.label: progressive myoclonus epilepsy
shortlist.why_kept: palatal myoclonus at 1-2 Hz and progressive ataxia

shortlist.label: cerebellar ataxia
shortlist.why_kept: truncal and limb ataxia, decreased vibratory sense, and inability to ambulate

shortlist.label: gaucher disease type 3
shortlist.why_kept: progressive ataxia and myoclonus, although genetic testing for other forms was normal

raw.rationale: The patient's 20-year history of progressive ataxia, truncal and limb ataxia, decreased vibratory sense, and severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy on MRI are consistent with cerebellar ataxia. The presence of palatal myoclonus also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: spinocerebellar ataxia
rejected.why: Genetic testing for spinocerebellar ataxia types 1, 2, 3, 6, and 12 was normal

rejected.label: progressive myoclonus epilepsy
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms do not include epilepsy or seizures

rejected.label: parkinsonism
rejected.why: While the patient has bradykinesia and mild rigidity, the primary symptoms are ataxia and myoclonus, which are not typical of parkinsonism

rejected.label: gaucher disease type 3
rejected.why: There is no mention of systemic symptoms or other characteristic features of Gaucher disease
